notes: newest release first; one entry per published Android arm64 bundle; the empty array is the bootstrap state
trust_chain: 1. this file is fetched over HTTPS from the public repository; there is no token, because a phone that needed a credential to read a release could not update itself
2. one entry pins one bundle by sha256(bundle.manifest), the same value the operator used to paste into install-termux.sh --manifest-sha256
3. the downloaded asset must be exactly the entry's size, or the transfer is refused (download_truncated)
4. sha256(downloaded bundle/bundle.manifest) must equal manifest_sha256, or the download is refused (hash_mismatch) and nothing is installed

5. the bundle then goes through the same verification a hand-installed bundle does: bundle.manifest describes installed.sha256, installed.sha256 describes every member, every artefact hash is checked, the ELF machine and the aarch64-linux-android triple are read from the bytes, and the candidate is run once before it is switched in
6. the trust anchor is the HTTPS origin of this file plus the committed history of the repository; a hash that does not match is a refusal, never a fallback to building
